A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage, despite a changed title and substantially revised method. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete supplementary material support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attention analyses, image and video benchmark evaluations, pruning ablations, and inference-efficiency measurements in Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–D.

after.justification: v2 reports original positional-attention controls, component ablations, benchmark comparisons, and efficiency measurements in Sections 3–5 and the supplementary material.

M1.justification: FasterVLM selects tokens solely through visual-encoder [CLS] attention. VisPruner adds iterative similarity-based duplicate removal to retain complementary diverse tokens, then combines and orders both token sets before inference (Section 4, Algorithm 1). It also introduces attention handling for encoders without [CLS] and for Qwen-VL's adapter. These are procedural changes beyond renaming.

E1.justification: The ten image benchmarks and broad image/video task families remain. However, ActivityNet-QA results and its supplementary dataset description disappear: v2 Table 3 and Section 7.1 support three video benchmarks, despite leftover four-benchmark wording elsewhere. Reported LLaVA-NeXT coverage also contracts from ten benchmarks to five.

E2.justification: The LLaVA-1.5 comparison adds ToMe, PruMerge+, and VisionZip alongside retained FastV and SparseVLM, while removing FitPrune from evaluation despite retaining its citation. VisionZip also joins the LLaVA-NeXT comparison. This substantially broadens comparison beyond text-visual attention methods.

E3.justification: Primary LLaVA-1.5-7B retained-token budgets change from 288/144/58/29 to 128/64/32, with corresponding budget revisions for high-resolution and video experiments. v2 adds Qwen-VL-7B, InternVL-Chat-13B, and CogVLM-chat-1.1-17B configurations and positional-intervention protocols. The SQA-IMG throughput evaluation disappears; POPE latency evaluation already existed in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: v2 adds layerwise quartile-retention tests, equal-position-embedding attention controls, and a qualitative hallucination case (Figures 1–3). Its fixed-budget component ablation tests the benefit of diverse tokens (Figure 5). v1's patch-attention, pruning-location, merging, and no-visual-input ablations are removed. The supplementary attention maps and layerwise distributions are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting remains unchanged; averaging attention over sampled examples is not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark results are extensively replaced and expanded. For example, v1 Table 1 reports 89.41% relative performance for FasterVLM with 29 tokens, whereas v2 reports 91.5% for VisPruner with 32; these different methods and budgets do not establish a same-setting gain. New architecture results appear, while ActivityNet-QA and detailed LLaVA-1.5-13B benchmark rows disappear. Supplementary efficiency Tables 6–8 retain v1 Tables 11–13's numerical entries under the new method name.

T1.justification: v1's limited theoretical computation analysis, including the prefill FLOPs-reduction derivation in Section 4.2 and Equation 8, is removed. v2 revises the formal token-selection definitions for important and diverse sets and explicitly includes rotary-position terms in its attention expression, without introducing a substantial theorem or proof framework.

C1.justification: The central contribution shifts from the sufficiency of [CLS]-attention-only pruning to preserving complementary important and diverse tokens. The abstract also replaces the approximately 90% performance-retention claim at 95% pruning with headline claims of 91% FLOPs and 75% latency reduction. The broader critique of text-visual attention remains.

C2.justification: v2 specifically attributes attention shift to rotary-position distance decay, refining v1's primarily unidirectional-attention explanation, and examines dispersion after controlling positional decay. It newly emphasizes background-information loss from attention-only selection and interprets its complementary selection as pruning according to spatial information density (Sections 4.2 and 6). These substantially revise the mechanism and failure-condition arguments.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 adds implementation-level pseudocode for normalized-token similarity, alternating token partitions, and iterative removal. v2 documents adapter-specific attention handling and changes the advertised code repository from FasterVLM to VisPruner. Most dataset and hardware disclosures carry over, while the numerical setting of the new important-token ratio r remains unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 repositions the contribution against concurrent visual-cue pruning, citing VisionZip, '[CLS] Token Tells Everything Needed for Training-Free Efficient MLLMs,' and 'A Stitch in Time Saves Nine.' Sections 2 and 6 distinguish its diversity-preserving design from attention-only selection and token merging. Added rotary-position literature also supports the revised explanation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, attention investigation, and method exposition are substantially rewritten. Related work is consolidated, the conclusion becomes a discussion, and the supplementary structure removes the additional-results section while reorganizing retained material. The title and method terminology also change throughout.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v2 introduces a qualitative opening figure, new multipart analysis plots, a redrawn method diagram, an algorithm listing, revised table structures, and component-ablation bars. Earlier radar plots and detailed supplementary benchmark tables disappear; supplementary attention figures and efficiency tables are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the central argument through positional controls, a fixed-budget diversity ablation, and comparisons with relevant visual-pruning alternatives. These evidential gains are limited by removed benchmark detail, the unspecified token-allocation hyperparameter, and unresolved efficiency reporting. In particular, the abstract claims 75% latency reduction for LLaVA-1.5-7B, whereas supplementary Table 6 shows about 28%; the approximately 75% reduction is reported for LLaVA-NeXT in Table 5.
